# IC-705 memory-record transcription (leg B)

## Source

- Document title as printed on the cover (PDF page 1): `CI-V REFERENCE GUIDE`, in the reversed band beneath the ICOM logo; below it `HF/VHF/UHF ALL MODE TRANSCEIVER` and `IC-705`; at the foot, `Icom Inc.`
- Revision code as printed: `A7560-8EX-6`, printed at the foot of the left-hand column of the last page (PDF page 31, no folio), immediately above `© 2020–2023  Icom Inc.    Jan. 2023`. The document prints no wording such as "Rev. 6" anywhere I read; the trailing `-6` of the document number is the only revision marker seen.
- File path: `/Users/stuart/Documents/working/coding/ft710-programmer.nosync/docs/fixtures-private/manuals/ic705_civ_rev6.pdf`
- Page count: 31 (established from the renderer itself: `-f 31 -l 31` renders; `-f 32 -l 32` is refused with "the first page (32) can not be after the last page (31)").

## Extent

Rendered at 300 dpi: PDF pages 8–21 (survey), plus PDF page 1 (cover) and PDF page 31 (last page) at 200 dpi for the ## Source facts. Re-rendered at 400 dpi: PDF pages 9, 19, 20. Re-rendered at 600 dpi: PDF page 19 (second pass).

Read closely, with the printed folio beside each:

| PDF page | printed folio | what it contributed |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | 8 | Nothing to the CSV. See "set-mode pages" below. |
| 19 | 18 | The whole of diagram D1 and every field entry, value list and inset transcribed. |
| 20 | 19 | The character table. See below. |

**Where the transcribed material begins and ends.** On PDF page 19 (folio 18) the material begins at the top of the page: running head `REMOTE CONTROL`, the reversed section band `Remote control (CI-V) information`, the sub-heading `◇ Command formats`, then the caption `• Memory content` (bold, bulleted) with `Command: 1A 00` beneath it, then the two-band data diagram. It ends with the shaded `NOTE:` box at the foot of the right-hand column, whose last line is "…We recommend that you set the same data as (6) ~ (52)." Nothing else is printed on that page; the folio `18` sits centred at the foot. The next material in the document, at the top of PDF page 20 (folio 19), is the caption `• Codes for character entries`, under the same `◇ Command formats` sub-heading — a different section, not transcribed as a diagram here.

**Diagram identification.** Only one distinct memory-record data-block diagram is printed:

- **D1** — printed caption `• Memory content`, with `Command: 1A 00` on the line beneath. It occupies the full page width immediately below that caption on PDF page 19, drawn as two bands: an upper band running left to right and a lower band reached by a wrap-around arrow that leaves the right-hand end of the upper band, loops below it, and re-enters the lower band from the left with a solid arrowhead. Both bands are one diagram and share one index sequence, so both are D1.

Three small inset boxes are printed further down the same page, under the legend entries for ⑤, ⑭ and ⑮. Each is captioned only by its own circled index numeral set above the box, and each expands one field that already has a row in the CSV. They are therefore folded into their field's row rather than given diagram ids of their own; giving them ids would have produced a second row for fields ⑤, ⑭ and ⑮, against the "one CSV row per numbered field" rule. Their content (the box cells, the leader lines and the value lists they point to) is transcribed in those rows.

**Character table — printed, and what it contributed.** Yes, it is printed, on PDF page 20 (folio 19), in the left-hand column under the caption `• Codes for character entries` and the command list `Command: 1A 00, / 1A 05 0168, 0288, 0308, 0310, / 0311, 0322, 0325, 0337, / 0345, / 1A 05 0291 ~ 1A 05 0294, / 1A 05 0297 ~ 1A 05 0300`. It comprises: a table headed `- Character codes— Letters and Numbers` with columns `Character` / `ASCII code` / `Character` / `ASCII code` and rows `A ~ Z` = `41 ~ 5A`, `a ~ z` = `61 ~ 7A`, `0 ~ 9` = `30 ~ 39` (the two right-hand cells of the second row are struck through with a diagonal rule); a second table headed `- Character codes— Symbols` of further Character/ASCII code pairs; and a third table with columns `Cmd.` / `Sub cmd.` / `Set item/selectable characters` whose first row reads `1A` / `00` / `Memory name` / `All characters are usable.` and whose second row reads `05` / `0168` / `NTP Server Address` / `A ~ Z, a ~ z, 0 ~ 9, ., -`.

  Its contribution: it is the only printed basis for `encoding = ascii` on the `(53)~(68)` memory-name row, since the `1A` `00` row names Memory name explicitly and the code columns are headed `ASCII code`. It contributed no other cell. It is the reason the three call-sign rows differ from the memory-name row: their cross-reference points to "DV TX call signs setting." (p. 23), which is outside the pages this leg read, so their encoding is recorded as `unstated` rather than `ascii`.

  Note that page 20 also prints a second small data diagram in its right-hand column, captioned `• Band stacking register` / `Command: 1A 01`, with two outline-circled indices ① and ② over a two-box `X X X X` band. It is a different command and is not a memory record, so it is not transcribed here; it is recorded only so a second reader knows it was seen and deliberately left out.

**Set-mode pages — printed, and what they contributed.** PDF page 9 (folio 8) is printed and was read. It is a `◇ Command table` spread: two four-column tables (`Cmd.` / `Sub cmd.` / `Data` / `Description`) of `1A*` `05` sub-commands `0116`–`0135` under the shaded band `SET > Connectors` and `0136`–`0144` under `SET > Display`. **It contributed nothing to the CSV**: no field of the Memory content diagram refers to set mode, to a menu item, or to any `1A 05` sub-command. Every cross-reference printed against a D1 field points instead to "Operating frequency." (p. 17), "Operating mode." (p. 17), "Duplex Offset frequency setting." (p. 17), "Repeater tone/tone squelch frequency setting." (p. 22), "DTCS code and polarity setting." (p. 22), "DV Digital code squelch setting." (p. 23), "DV TX call signs setting." (p. 23) or "Codes for character entries." (p. 19). Those are printed folios; only the last of them, folio 19 = PDF page 20, is within this leg's pages, and it is the character table above. The other referenced pages were not opened, so where a field's only printed content is such a cross-reference, `values_verbatim` is empty and the cross-reference is quoted in `notes`. That emptiness is a finding: **on the page that defines them, fields (6)~(10), (11), (12), (16)~(18), (19)~(21), (22)~(24), (25), (26)~(28), (29)~(36), (37)~(44), (45)~(52), (53)~(68) and ●6 ~ ●52 have no value, code or range printed at all.**

## Method

1. **Locate.** `pdftoppm -png -r 300 -f 8 -l 21 <pdf> r300/p` into the fresh directory `.../evidence/ic705-B/r300`, created for this task; nothing pre-existed in it. Cover and last page: `pdftoppm -png -r 200 -f 1 -l 1` and `-f 31 -l 31`. The whole-page renders were read as images to find the sections; the section whose printed caption is `• Memory content` (PDF page 19) is the only one worked in for the diagram, and `• Codes for character entries` (PDF page 20) the only one worked in for the character table.
2. **Read (pass 1).** `pdftoppm -png -r 400 -f 9 -l 9` and `-f 19 -l 20` into `r400/`. Every pass-1 value was read from crops of `r400/p-19.png` and `r400/p-20.png`.
3. **Crop and enlarge.** ImageMagick **was** available (`/opt/homebrew/bin/magick`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/convert`) and was used throughout. Pass-1 commands, all against `r400/p-19.png` unless stated:
   - band 1 whole: `-crop 2700x260+200+1000 +repage -resize 200%`
   - band 1 in three overlapping windows: `-crop 900x230+230+1010`, `+1100+1010`, `+1950+1010`, each `+repage -resize 350%`
   - band 2 whole: `-crop 2700x300+200+1250 +repage -resize 200%`; band 2 in three windows at `+250+1250`, `+1030+1250`, `+1810+1250`, each `830x300 +repage -resize 350%`
   - left legend column in four bands: `-crop 1500x800+220+1500`, `+220+2280`, `+220+3060`, `+220+3840`, each `+repage -resize 200%`
   - right legend column in four bands: `-crop 1550x760+1690+1500`, `+1690+2240`, `+1690+2980`, and `1550x800+1690+3720`, each `+repage -resize 200%`
   - the ⑮ glyph twice: `-crop 130x110+1595+1085 +repage -resize 600%` (band) and the inset within the `+220+3840` band
   - page headings: `-crop 2000x600+230+400 +repage -resize 150%`
   - page 20: `-crop 1620x520+230+1430 +repage -resize 220%` (letters/numbers table) and `-crop 1620x420+230+3560 +repage -resize 220%` (Cmd. table)
   Every numeral, bracket end, box rule and shading boundary was legible at these enlargements; nothing had to be read from a whole-page render.
4. **`pdftotext`.** Not run. Not at all, in any form, on this or any other file.
5. **`tesseract`.** Available at `/opt/homebrew/bin/tesseract` but **not used**. Every value was read by eye from the enlarged crops.
6. **Second independent pass — done.** After pass 1 was complete, PDF page 19 was re-rendered at **600 dpi** (`pdftoppm -png -r 600 -f 19 -l 19` into `r600/`) — a different raster from the 400 dpi one every pass-1 value came from — and re-read through **different crop windows at a different enlargement**: the two bands were cut into **four** windows each (pass 1 used three), on different boundaries (`-crop 1060x400+380+1500`, `+1380`, `+2380`, `+3380` for band 1; `1060x420+…+1870` for band 2), enlarged **250%** (pass 1 used 350%); the left legend was re-cut into **five** bands of `2200x900` at 150% (pass 1: four bands at 200%) and the right legend into **four** bands of `2400x950` at 150%. Page 20's tables were re-read from `r400` crops at 220% and 250% on different boundaries from the survey read at 300 dpi.
   **Disagreements between the two passes: none.** Every index numeral and its style, every bracket span, every box count, every shading run, every label, every value string and every leader-line destination came out the same in both passes. The one cell I had specifically doubted after pass 1 — the second character of the ⑮ box, `O` or `0` — resolved the same way in both passes and at 600% enlargement: it is the digit `0`, identical in outline to the zero of `0=Digital squelch function OFF` printed a few lines below it, and the inset for ⑮ prints the same glyph with a leader labelled `Fixed`. No third render was needed for any cell.

**Transcription conventions** (needed because the printed index glyphs are not all encodable):
- an outline-circled numeral `n` is written `(n)`; a filled, reversed (white-on-black) circled numeral `n` is written `●n`. Unicode has no filled circled numerals above 20 and no circled numerals above 50, so the printed glyphs for 52, 53 and 68 cannot be reproduced directly.
- `field_index` uses the spacing of the **legend** entry (tight tildes, e.g. `(16)~(18)`). The diagram band prints the same ranges with spaces around the tilde (`(16) ~ (18)`). The one index that has no legend entry, `●6 ~ ●52`, is given in the band's spacing because that is the only place it is printed.
- a label set across two lines is joined with one space, as instructed (the three call-sign labels).
- alignment gaps (the run of spaces after `0100:`) are reproduced as a single space, and this is noted in the row.
- bullet markers (`•`) before list items inside a value list are not reproduced.
- directory access: the only directories touched were the render and evidence directories created for this task beneath `.../evidence/ic705-B`, holding my own renders and my own two output files. No repository directory, no manuals directory and no other directory was listed, searched or browsed, and no file outside that evidence directory was opened other than the one PDF named above.
- `pdfinfo` was run once on that same PDF at the outset, before any page was read. Nothing it printed is recorded anywhere in this deliverable: the page count in ## Source was re-established from `pdftoppm`'s own refusal of page 32, and the document title read from the rendered cover image rather than from metadata.

## Hazards encountered

- **(a) Numeral styling varies within one diagram — ENCOUNTERED.** Every index on D1 is an outline-circled numeral except one bracket in the lower band, whose two numerals are **filled, reversed circles** (white numeral on a solid black disc): `●6 ~ ●52`. The same two styles are used in the surrounding prose: the NOTE box prints outline `(6) ~ (52)` and filled `●6 ~ ●52` in the same sentence. Both styles are recorded as drawn; neither has been normalised to the other, and no meaning has been inferred for either beyond what the NOTE box itself prints. See STOP 2.
- **(b) Vector groups with rotated labels — NOT ENCOUNTERED.** Every label on and around D1 is set horizontally; nothing is rotated or mirrored. Position was in any case read from the picture throughout: each bracket was followed from its left leg to its right V by eye across the enlarged crop, and the boxes it spans counted on the render.
- **(c) Leader-line label order reversed — ENCOUNTERED.** In both the ⑤ inset and the ⑭ inset the two arrows cross the reading order: the arrow rising from the **right-hand** nibble runs right to the **upper** bracketed list (⑤: `0=OFF*`…`3= ★3`; ⑭: `0=OFF`…`3=DTCS`), whilst the arrow rising from the **left-hand** nibble runs down and right to the **lower** label (⑤: `0=Split OFF,1=Split ON`; ⑭: `0=Duplex OFF`…`2=Duplex+`). Read top to bottom, the labels therefore describe the second nibble before the first. Each leader was followed by eye from label to the cell it lands on, in both passes; the values are listed in the CSV in printed top-to-bottom order and the mapping is spelled out in each row's `notes`. The ⑮ inset does not reverse: its `Fixed` leader lands on the second cell, which is the cell printed as a literal `0`.
- **(d) Printed index differs from measured position — ENCOUNTERED.** The lower band's repeat block is printed `●6 ~ ●52` but measures at byte positions **53–99**, and the group printed `(53)~(68)` measures at byte positions **100–115**. Both the printed index and the measured position are recorded for every row and are not reconciled: `field_index` carries the index exactly as printed, and each row's `notes` carries the byte positions measured on the render by counting boxes from the start of the upper band (1 index = 1 box = 1 byte, the convention the un-elided groups establish).

## STOP findings

1. **Two different fields carry the identical printed label, and the cross-reference they share names two different settings.** PDF page 19, right-hand legend column, first two lines: `⑯~⑱: Repeater tone frequency setting` and, immediately below it, `⑲~㉑: Repeater tone frequency setting` — word for word the same, for two distinct three-byte ranges. The single cross-reference printed beneath them both reads `ⓘSee “Repeater tone/tone squelch frequency setting.” (p. 22)`, naming *two* settings (repeater tone, and tone squelch) for the two ranges. What is printed thus contradicts itself: either the two ranges are the same setting, in which case the diagram has two of them, or they are different settings, in which case one label is wrong. This is transcribed exactly as printed — both rows carry `Repeater tone frequency setting` — and neither has been "corrected" to tone squelch. Rows `(16)~(18)` and `(19)~(21)`, `notes` = `STOP 1`.
2. **The index sequence repeats indices 6 to 52, out of order, in a second styling.** PDF page 19, lower band, the wide dashed shaded ellipsis box between the `(45)~(52)` group and the `(53)~(68)` group. Its bracket is labelled with two **filled** circled numerals reading `6` and `52`, so the band's index sequence runs …45~52, **6~52**, 53~68. That is a repeat (6 to 52 already appeared in the upper band and the start of the lower band), it is out of order, and the same numerals 6 and 52 are printed twice on the one diagram in two different stylings — three of the listed discontinuity conditions at once. The page's own NOTE box states the relationship ("The same data as (6) ~ (52) are stored in ●6 ~ ●52.") but never labels the block, never gives it a width, and never states its byte position. The index is transcribed exactly as drawn, `●6 ~ ●52`, with the printed index and the measured positions 53–99 both recorded and not reconciled. Row `●6 ~ ●52`, `notes` = `STOP 2`.

No other STOP arose, and I record the reasons for that confidence: the arithmetic closes exactly — the widths in the CSV run 2+2+1+5+2+1+1+1+3+3+3+1+3+8+8+8+47+16 = 115 bytes with no gap and no overlap, every field abutting its neighbour on the render, and the box-and-shading pattern (adjacent fields alternate white and shaded fill) confirms every bracket boundary independently of the brackets themselves. Every numeral, rule and glyph was legible at 400 dpi enlarged, and nothing was recorded as `UNREADABLE`. The two passes did not disagree on any cell.

## Observed disagreements

Recorded as printed, not resolved, and not sufficient to stop the transcription:

1. **The elided groups draw fewer boxes than they have indices.** `(6)~(10)` is drawn as two `X X` boxes with a dashed ellipsis box between them — 3 boxes for 5 indices; `(29)~(36)`, `(37)~(44)`, `(45)~(52)` and `(53)~(68)` are each drawn as 3 boxes for 8, 8, 8 and 16 indices; `●6 ~ ●52` is drawn as a single box for 47. The un-elided groups (`(16)~(18)`, `(19)~(21)`, `(22)~(24)`, `(26)~(28)`, and every single-index field) draw exactly one box per index, which is what establishes the one-index-one-byte convention the widths rest on. The dashed border and the ellipsis of dots are the page's own abbreviation mark, so this is not treated as an arithmetic failure — but the drawn box count and the index count do differ, and each affected row says so.
2. **The band and the legend disagree about whether ⑪ and ⑫ are one field or two.** In the band, `(11)` and `(12)` are printed as two separate labels, one over each box, in the same style as the single-index fields; the legend prints them as one paired entry, `⑪, ⑫: Operating mode setting`. `(1), (2)` and `(3), (4)` are consistent between band and legend — each is a pair under one bracket in both.
3. **Tilde spacing differs between band and legend.** The band prints `(16) ~ (18)`, the legend `⑯~⑱`; likewise for every range. The clear-command block prints `(0000~0099)` with tight tildes where the main entry prints `0000 ~ 0099` with spaces.
4. **The cross-reference capitalises a word the label does not.** The field entry reads `㉖~㉘: Duplex offset frequency setting` (lower-case *offset*); the line below reads `ⓘSee “Duplex Offset frequency setting.” (p. 17)` (capital *Offset*).
5. **The clear-command range is open-ended.** The last line of the clear block reads `⑤: “FF,” ⑥ ~ : None` — a range that begins at ⑥ and prints no end index, so the document does not state which fields the value `None` covers. The line is transcribed in full in the `(5)` row (the line as printed is one line) and flagged in the `(6)~(10)` row's `notes`; `None` has not been attributed to any particular later field.
6. **The repeat block has no label at all.** No entry for `●6 ~ ●52` appears in either legend column; the only prose about it is the NOTE box. Its `label_verbatim` is therefore empty. That absence is a finding, not a gap: nothing was carried over from the counterpart fields `(6)`–`(52)` to fill it, as the instructions require.
7. **The ⑮ box prints a literal in a data cell.** Alone among the boxes in the bands, the ⑮ box prints `X 0` rather than `X X`; the inset repeats it and labels the second cell `Fixed`.

## Attestation

Nothing beyond this single PDF's rendered page images was consulted. No other file, manual, transcription, source file, generated artefact or web resource was opened, and no directory was listed.
